rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the key uncertainty is whether a well-motivated multimodal configuration can achieve strong validation accuracy, and which component choices matter most. config_009 (multimodal, singleprofile, scgpt, resnet50, weighted fusion) tests a strong, standard multimodal setup: a learned RNA encoder (scgpt) that should capture nonlinear biological signal better than PCA, a well-validated image encoder (resnet50), and a simple robust weighted fusion. This is the best first experiment because it establishes a high-quality reference point in the multimodal space with minimal architectural complexity (singleprofile, no aggregation step), making it easier to diagnose which axis to push next (multiprofile, transformer aggregation, ViT-L image encoder, concat fusion, scvi_n200) if performance is promising, or to identify a weak modality if it underperforms.

With only one completed experiment (config_009: multimodal, singleprofile, scgpt+resnet50, weighted fusion → 42.1% accuracy), the critical uncertainty is how much each modality contributes individually. Config_028 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) isolates the image branch using the exact same image encoder and profile setting as config_009, enabling a direct comparison. If image-only accuracy is near 42%, RNA adds little and the fusion strategy is the bottleneck; if it is substantially lower, RNA is a meaningful contributor and we should focus on improving RNA encoding or fusion. Resolving this modality-contribution question early is essential for allocating the remaining 8 experiments efficiently toward the right design dimensions (fusion, multiprofile, encoder upgrades) rather than chasing a modality that may be underperforming.

Evidence: config_009 (multimodal, scgpt+resnet50, weighted fusion) achieved 0.421 acc, while config_028 (image_only, resnet50) achieved only 0.208 acc — a 21-point gap showing RNA is critical. However, we cannot yet decompose how much of the 0.421 comes from RNA alone versus the multimodal combination. Question: config_038 (rna_only, singleprofile, scgpt) is a clean ablation of config_009 that isolates the RNA contribution. If RNA alone approaches ~0.40+, the image modality adds little and remaining budget should target RNA encoder/architecture improvements. If RNA alone is much lower (~0.20-0.30), the multimodal fusion is genuinely synergistic and we should prioritize multiprofile aggregation and fusion strategy experiments. With only 2 data points, this decomposition is the highest-information experiment to guide the remaining 7 trials efficiently.

Evidence: config_009 (multimodal, scgpt+resnet50, weighted) achieves 0.4214, while RNA-only scgpt (config_038) achieves 0.4106 and image-only resnet50 (config_028) is very weak at 0.2079. This shows RNA is the dominant signal and the image modality contributes only ~1% via resnet50. Question: Is the weak image contribution due to a suboptimal image encoder? config_002 swaps resnet50 for imagenet_vit_l while keeping everything else identical to config_009 (scgpt, singleprofile, weighted fusion), making it a clean single-variable test. Why this is the best next experiment: With 6 experiments remaining, isolating the image encoder variable is the highest-information experiment—if imagenet_vit_l substantially boosts image signal, the multimodal model could see a meaningful accuracy gain; if not, we can confidently rule out image encoder quality as the bottleneck and redirect remaining budget toward multiprofile aggregation or RNA encoder alternatives.

All four completed experiments used singleprofile, so the impact of multiprofile aggregation is the largest unexplored design dimension. Our best results (config_009: 0.4214, config_002: 0.4224) both use scgpt + weighted fusion in multimodal mode, with only a marginal difference between resnet50 and imagenet_vit_l. Config_019 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) is the most controlled extension of our best singleprofile config: it keeps the same RNA encoder, image encoder, and fusion strategy while introducing multiprofile with a simple, robust avgpool aggregation. This isolates the effect of multi-profile aggregation and tells us whether capturing multiple spatial profiles can push accuracy beyond the ~0.42 plateau. With 5 experiments remaining, resolving whether multiprofile is a productive direction is critical before committing further budget to more complex variants (transformer aggregation, different encoders).

The best result so far is config_019 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) at 0.5251 accuracy, showing a large jump over singleprofile configs (~0.42). The key uncertainty is whether the aggregation method (avgpool vs. transformer) can further improve performance in the multiprofile setting. Config_013 makes a single-variable change from the best config—replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping scgpt, resnet50, and weighted fusion fixed. Transformer aggregation can model complex inter-profile interactions that simple averaging cannot, making it a high-impact architectural question. With only 4 experiments remaining after this, resolving the aggregation choice is critical: if transformer helps, subsequent experiments can combine it with other improvements (e.g., VIT-L, concat fusion); if it doesn't, we confirm avgpool is optimal and pivot to other variables. This is the most informative next step to exploit the multiprofile direction while reducing uncertainty about the best aggregation strategy.

The current best (config_019, acc=0.5251) uses multimodal + multiprofile + scgpt + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted. The singleprofile experiments showed imagenet_vit_l was marginally better than resnet50 (0.4224 vs 0.4214), but the difference was small when only one image embedding was used. With multiprofile avgpool, multiple image embeddings are averaged, so a richer per-profile image representation (ViT-L) could provide more discriminative features to aggregate, potentially yielding a larger gain. config_037 is a clean one-variable change (resnet50→imagenet_vit_l) from the best config, keeping the proven avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion. This is the highest-value exploitation step: if it improves, we lock in a stronger baseline for the remaining 3 experiments to further refine (e.g., testing concat fusion or scvi_n200); if it doesn't, we confirm resnet50 is sufficient and can pivot to other axes.

The current best is config_037 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted; acc=0.542). All top-performing configs use weighted fusion, but concat fusion has never been tested with this strongest backbone (scgpt + ViT-L + avgpool + multiprofile). Config_014 is a clean single-variable ablation of config_037 (only fusion changes from weighted to concat), directly testing whether concatenating the two modality representations before the classifier could outperform the weighted sum. This is the highest-value exploitation step: if concat wins, we get a new best with 2 experiments left to further refine; if it doesn't, we confirm weighted fusion is optimal and can spend remaining budget exploring RNA encoder alternatives (e.g., scvi_n200) or aggregation strategies with full confidence in the fusion choice.

The best configuration so far is config_037 (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) at 0.542 accuracy. The strongest evidence shows multiprofile + avgpool + weighted fusion + imagenet_vit_l is the optimal architecture. However, the RNA encoder (scgpt) has only been tested in this best setup; scvi_n200, a learned variational embedding, remains untested in this exact configuration. Config_046 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) directly tests whether an alternative RNA encoder can match or exceed scgpt in the best-performing architecture. This is the highest-value single-variable change: if scvi_n200 performs comparably, it confirms the architecture is the bottleneck; if it exceeds scgpt, we find a new best. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, testing the most impactful untested variable (RNA encoder) in the proven best setup is the best use of the budget to either improve on 0.542 or confirm the ceiling.

The best result (config_046, acc=0.706) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted. The evidence strongly supports these three components (scvi_n200 >> scgpt >> pca; vit_l > resnet50; avgpool > transformer). The only untested variation within this strongest base is the fusion strategy. For scgpt, weighted slightly outperformed concat (0.542 vs 0.518), but scvi_n200 produces richer, higher-dimensional latent representations where concatenation may preserve more discriminative information than weighted averaging. Config_042 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + concat) is the single most logical extension of the best result, testing whether the fusion preference reverses with the stronger RNA encoder. As the final experiment, this maximizes the chance of either confirming the current best or discovering a marginally better configuration.
